newsitem.title: AFGHANISTAN: No Afghan ceasefire agreed, says Masood spokesman.
newsitem.headline: No Afghan ceasefire agreed, says Masood spokesman.

text.p: A spokesman for the ousted government of Afghanistan said on Monday ceasefire negotiations in the northern city of Mazar-i-Sharif had failed.

"They (faction leaders) have not agreed on a ceasefire," Dr Abdullah (one name), spokesman for Ahmad Shah Masood, the commander of ousted government forces, told reporters in Jabal os-Siraj. "They (Taleban militia) are still bombing so the ceasefire that was proposed has not taken place," he said.

Abdullah said two Taleban warplanes had dropped bombs on the village of Qarabagh on Monday. Reporters heard anti-aircraft fire open up from Masood's forces at jets earlier in the day but no casualties were confirmed.

Abdullah said skirmishes between ousted government forces and the radical Islamic Taleban militia, who hold the Afghan capital Kabul, had continued throughout the day around 15 km (10 miles) north of the city. Occasional rocket fire could be heard from Jabal os-Siraj as darkness fell.
Asked if he was optimistic about any further attempts to negotiate a ceasefire, Abdullah said, "Personally, no".
Many of Masood's men, among whom morale is high, want to move on the city.
